AC1 and design step 2 only exclude a digit immediately before '8=FIX' (and a delimiter earlier on the line); any other prefix text is ignored, so a prefix such as '1=ABC ' or '58=' hides the message.
reported.failure: splitMessages("1=ABC 8=FIX.4.4|9=5|35=0|10=123|") returns [] (no candidate at all). The character before '8=FIX' at offset 6 is a space and the line before it contains no delimiter, so AC1 requires one candidate with start 6 and fields 8,9,35,10. Same for "58=8=FIX.4.4|9=5|35=0|10=123|": prev is '=' so the hit at offset 3 is skipped and [] is returned.

reported.spec_ref: a candidate starts at `8=FIX` when the character before it is not a digit and the line before it contains no delimiter (design section 3, step 2).

BeginString values that do not begin with '.' or 'T' are dropped here instead of being framed and later labelled 'unsupported version' (section 5).

Now that AC3 splits a checksum-less candidate at the next start, the first candidate is reported with the second candidate's rule and a position outside its own boundary.

reported.claim: The checksum is summed over the original pasted text (text.substring(start, lastField.position)), not over the normalised copy where the line delimiter is SOH. On a pipe-delimited line every '|' contributes 124 instead of 1, so a paste of a real SOH message rendered with '|' is reported as a checksum mismatch.
reported.failure: splitMessages("8=FIX.4.4|9=5|35=0|10=163|") gives one candidate; checkMessage returns {rule:"checksum", position:20, text:"Message 1: CheckSum mismatch at position 20"} because it computes 020 over the pipes. On the SOH-normalised text the byte sum is 931, 931 % 256 = 163, so the message is valid and checkMessage must return null (body_length already passes: 5).
reported.test_idea: test('pipe paste of an SOH message is valid', () => { const soh = "8=FIX.4.4\x019=5\x0135=0\x0110=163\x01"; const pipe = soh.replaceAll("\x01", "|"); expect(checkMessage(splitMessages(pipe)[0], pipe)).toBeNull(); });
reported.spec_ref: the sum of the UTF-8 bytes of the normalised text from the message start up to and including the SOH before `10=`, modulo 256 and written as 3 digits, isn't the value of tag 10: `checksum`.
